{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Southern Natural Gas (SNG) Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2kjZgVD Southern Natural Gas (SNG) Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from natural gas supply basins in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and the Gulf of Mexico to markets in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina and Tennessee.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/southern-company-kinder-morgan-enter-southern-natural-gas-pipeline-strategic-venture-300296288.html|title=Southern Company, Kinder Morgan enter Southern Natural Gas pipeline strategic venture|last=|first=|date=10 July, 2016|website=PR Newswire|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=30 August, 2023}}</ref>

==Background==
The Southern Natural Gas Pipeline system is operated by Kinder Morgan Energy Partners, and owned by Kinder Morgan (50%) and Southern Company (50%).<ref name=":0" />

===Cypress Pipeline Project===
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission noticed the Cypress Pipeline Project in July 2005. The project would be built in three phases with in-service dates of May 1, 2007, May 2009 and May 2010.<ref name="r820af0" />

The first phase was completed in May 2007 at a reported cost of $240 million.<ref name="r30800f" />

===North Alabama Pipeline===
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission voted 5-0 on May 28, 1997 to grant Southern Natural Gas a certificate for about 118 miles of pipeline to serve Huntsville and Decatur, Alabama. The commission described the project as controversial.<ref name="raa712b" />

===South System Expansion I Project, Phase 1===


===South System Expansion II Phase 1A===


===South System Expansion III Project, Phase 1===


===South System Expansion II Phase 3===

===South System Expansion 4 Project===
The South System Expansion 4 Project was developed by Southern Natural Gas Company and its affiliate Elba Express Company. Southern Natural Gas is equally owned by subsidiaries of Kinder Morgan and Southern Company, and Elba Express is a Kinder Morgan subsidiary.<ref name="r1a503a" /> The companies began the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission pre-filing process on October 30, 2024 and filed a certificate application on June 30, 2025.<ref name="r1a503a" /> The project adds about 1.3 Bcf/d of firm capacity on the Southern Natural Gas South Main Line, at an estimated cost of about $3.5 billion.<ref name="r1a503a" />

The project is almost entirely looping and compression additions on existing assets. A Kinder Morgan fact sheet gave about 290 miles of looping, mainly 42-inch, 36-inch and 30-inch pipe.<ref name="r1a503a" /> Pipeline & Gas Journal reported in August 2026 that the plan has 22 loops totaling about 291 miles across Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia.<ref name="rbc6446" /> The commission approved the project on July 31, 2026.<ref name="rbc6446" /><ref name="rea6cd1" /> Kinder Morgan expects the first phase to enter service in the fourth quarter of 2028 and the second phase in the fourth quarter of 2029.<ref name="rea6cd1" /> A 2025 fact sheet had anticipated construction starting in the fourth quarter of 2026.<ref name="r1a503a" />

===Southeast Connector Project===
Southern Natural Gas Company announced a binding open season for the Southeast Connector Project on September 16, 2026. The open season closed on October 7, 2026.<ref name="r709022" /> The project adds a new supply line that would take gas in Tennessee from four pipelines. It also expands the Southern Natural Gas system in Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina and Florida.<ref name="r709022" /> The notice gave a target in-service date of November 1, 2030, with all service starting no later than November 1, 2032.<ref name="r709022" />

Kinder Morgan reported in October 2026 that Southern Natural Gas had made a final investment decision on the project. The project is designed to carry up to 2.6 Bcf/d through about 470 miles of new pipeline plus new and expanded compression.<ref name="r3e47cd" /> Service is expected to start in phases from the fourth quarter of 2030, subject to permits and approvals. Kinder Morgan put its own share of the cost at $3.1 billion.<ref name="r3e47cd" /> WPLN News reported in October 2026 that about 150 of the 470 miles are in Tennessee, running from Sumner County to Marion County. It gave the pipe diameter as 48 inches and said capacity could grow to 3.5 Bcf/d.<ref name="r3ba493" />
